answer: Timber Beacon Protocol Each agent must prove continuous presence by submitting a signed digest derived from a public beacon every 10 minutes. The beacon is a cryptographically secure hash chain updated every minute, seeded by a trusted comet orbiting Earth. Agents derive their contribution using a keyed hash of the current beacon value and their private key. To forge multiple identities, an attacker must predict future beacon states—impossible without breaking SHA-3’s preimage resistance.
